items.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.pt: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings;

items.pt: Vision-language models still struggle to understand 3D spatial relations across views and update spatial judgments as the observer moves.
